newsitem.title: UK: Skiers told they endanger wallets as well as limbs.
newsitem.headline: Skiers told they endanger wallets as well as limbs.

text.p: For skiers enjoying the thrill of the world's pistes, a fall might cost an arm and a leg but Europeans could come a real financial cropper in the United States.
A leading insurance company warned in a news release on Wednesday that visitors to winter resorts forked out hundreds of thousands of dollars each year for emergency medical assistance.

UK-based Europ Assistance said the cost of treatment varied dramatically from country to country. It can cost nearly five times more to break your leg in the U.S. than in France if you are a European Union citizen, it added.

A skier injured in Colorado, for example, could face bills of 7,047 stg ($11,900) in medical expenses, plus 2,177 stg for air tickets, and another 36 stg for an ambulance or taxi - a total of 9,261 stg.

At Alpes d'Huez in France, where EU citizens qualify for state healthcare, medical costs would be 101 stg, but with 981 stg in airline tickets, 489 stg in ambulances, and 212 in other expenses - a total of 1,785 stg.
